title: Expectile vs mean neighbor aggregation on a tail-shifted contextual SBM
setting: Synthetic 2-class stochastic block graph (600 nodes, average degree 10) with tunable homophily. Node features are 6-dimensional; class 1 has an upper-tail mixture while class 0 is Gaussian, with mean and variance matched across classes plus a tiny class shift, so class information in neighborhoods lies mostly in skew/tail shape. Per-node neighbor aggregation (with self-loop; mean or expectile via 20 fixed-point iterations) is concatenated with the node's own features and fed to a logistic regression (C chosen on validation) on a 60/20/20 split; the metric is test accuracy.

paper.title: Graph Representation Learning via Adaptive Expectile Aggregation
paper.claim: Expectile aggregation can exploit class-dependent distributional differences (e.g., tail/scale) in heterophilic neighborhoods to beat mean aggregation, with mean as the tau=0.5 special case.

metric.name: test_acc
metric.description: Accuracy on held-out test nodes (20% of nodes) of the logistic readout on [self features, aggregated neighbor features].

factors.name: method
factors.description: mean: mean aggregation. expectile: tau selected on validation accuracy from {0.5,0.1,0.25,0.75,0.9} (stand-in for learnable tau; ties go to the mean). expectile_fixed: tau=0.9 without selection.

factors.name: homophily
factors.description: Probability that a neighbor shares the node's class. 0.5 makes neighbor class labels uninformative; 0.2 and 0.8 are heterophilic and homophilic.

factors.name: tail_frac
factors.description: Fraction of class-1 feature values drawn from the large positive mode (strength of the tail signal).

factors.name: noise
factors.description: Std of Gaussian corruption added to all node features.
